statement: Whenever count_good_integers(n,k) returns a result r, r is the number of integers x such that 10^(n-1) <= x <= 10^n - 1 and there exists an integer y such that: (i) y has exactly n decimal digits, i.e. 10^(n-1) <= y <= 10^n - 1; (ii) the multiset of decimal digits of y equals the multiset of decimal digits of x; (iii) y is a palindrome (its n decimal digits read the same forwards and backwards); and (iv) k divides y. Equivalently, r is the number of n-digit positive integers whose digits can be rearranged, without leading zero in the rearranged number, into an n-digit palindrome divisible by k. Each such integer x is counted once, no matter how many witness rearrangements y exist.
preconditions: n and k are the integer values of the parameters, with 1 <= n <= 10 and 1 <= k <= 9.

statement: For every n and k satisfying the preconditions, count_good_integers(n,k) returns a result (it does not fail, panic, or overflow).
preconditions: n and k are the integer values of the parameters, with 1 <= n <= 10 and 1 <= k <= 9.

statement: Whenever count_good_integers(n,k) returns a result r, one has 1 <= r <= 9 * 10^(n-1).
preconditions: n and k are the integer values of the parameters, with 1 <= n <= 10 and 1 <= k <= 9.

statement: When n = 1, if count_good_integers(1,k) returns r, then r is the number of d in {1,2,...,9} such that k divides d; equivalently r = floor(9/k).
preconditions: n and k are the integer values of the parameters, with n = 1 and 1 <= k <= 9.

statement: Whenever count_good_integers(n,k1) returns r1 and count_good_integers(n,k2) returns r2, we have r2 <= r1.
preconditions: n, k1, and k2 are integers with 1 <= n <= 10, 1 <= k1 <= 9, 1 <= k2 <= 9, and k1 divides k2.
